ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows triangle XYZ, with a right-angle mark at vertex Y; side XY is labeled 15, and side XZ is labeled 25. Because the right angle is at Y, the side XZ opposite the right angle is the hypotenuse. ∠Z is required. Relative to angle Z, the opposite side is XY = 15, and the hypotenuse is XZ = 25, therefore use the sine ratio: sin(Z) = 15/25 = 0.6. Thus Z = arcsin(0.6) ≈ 36.8699°, rounded to the nearest tenth as 36.9°.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify triangle XYZ with a right-angle marker at Y, side XY labeled 15, and side XZ labeled 25. Since XZ is opposite the right angle, treat XZ as the hypotenuse. The text asks for the measure of angle Z to the nearest tenth. Use the sine ratio relative to angle Z: the side opposite angle Z is XY = 15 and the hypotenuse is XZ = 25, so sin(Z) = 15/25 = 0.6. Compute Z = arcsin(0.6) and round to the nearest tenth, giving 36.9 degrees.
